title: Quant tuning retrospective with EHR Platform
summary: Walkthrough of Optimize console quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) for ClearHealth's clinical summarization workload; discussed latency/quality tradeoffs, rollout plan (canary -> phased), security requirements (VPC + KMS), and a plan to run a 2-week pilot with prioritized prompt set. Agreed on benchmarks, success criteria, and next steps to share security whitepaper and run a 1000-sample fidelity sweep.
action_items: Priya: send pilot pricing sheet and pilot contract template by 2026-06-11
Maya: share 3 canonical prompt sets and sample patient records (anonymized) by 2026-06-12
Liam: spin up a benchmark harness and provide baseline latency numbers for INT8/FP8 by 2026-06-15
Alex: confirm VPC peering window with infra team by 2026-06-14
next_steps: Schedule pilot kickoff (2 weeks) - tentative start 2026-06-17
Run fidelity sweep on 1k examples focusing on hallucination/clinical accuracy
Share security and SOC2 docs, KMS integration guide
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-09 15:30 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Liam (SE), Nora (Product) -- Maya (ClearHealth ML Lead), Alex (Platform), Samir (Security)

[00:00] Priya: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you all hear me ok?
[00:04] Maya: yeah loud and clear, thanks Priya.
[00:06] Alex: yep good here.
[00:09] Priya: great, so quick agenda — walk through the Optimize console quant profile UI, show a short benchmark of int8 vs fp8 on your summarization workload, then talk rollout plans and security checklists. if anything we can pause.
[00:22] Liam: (screen share) ok i'm in the console, jumping to the "Quant Profiles" tab — this is where you can create named profiles, set per-layer tolerances, and attach them to a route or model version. note that we have recommended presets: conservative-int8, balanced-int8, exploratory-fp8.
[00:39] Nora: curious — for clinical text we usually prioritize fidelity over throughput, but cost matters too. how should we think about these presets?
[00:47] Liam: good question. conservative-int8 trades a bit more latency savings for slightly safer weight clipping heuristics; balanced-int8 gives you more compression without as big a hit; fp8 gives better representational fidelity at similar or slightly higher compute on newer kernels. in our internal runs fp8 typically yields better token-level perplexity on medical text, but some workloads see minimal delta.
[01:12] Maya: when you say "fp8 better perplexity" does that translate to fewer hallucinations in summaries? that is the metric we really care about.
[01:18] Liam: yes often, but not guaranteed. perplexity correlates with fluency and sometimes factuality; for hallucination you want targeted evals — we recommend a prompt-based eval suite with clinical facts checks. we ran a small sweep on v2 of your model across 500 notes — fp8 reduced hallucination flags by about 7% compared to balanced-int8 in that run.
[01:41] Samir: quick security interjection — any change to numeric formats or model graphs impacts our auditability? we need to ensure we can reproduce runs for compliance.
[01:48] Priya: absolutely. on Redwood Private or Dedicated we provide deterministic run logs, seed settings, and model-config snapshots. our Optimize console logs the quant profile used, kernel variants, and the exact model sha. and we have KMS-wrapped keys for model artifacts.
[02:07] Samir: okay and that includes audit trail for which profile was used per request?
[02:11] Nora: yes the token-level trace in the Console includes route -> model version -> quant profile id, and you can export that for audits.
[02:19] Alex: are there any latency numbers you can share for our expected p95? our SLAs are pretty tight — 200ms p95 for short summarizations (~150 tokens).
[02:29] Liam: for your infra and sample sizes, on A100s with batched inference at batch size 8 — conservative-int8 was hitting ~180ms p95 on 150-token sequences; balanced-int8 ~150ms; fp8 ~165ms but with higher memory pressure so it may limit burst concurrency. these vary with batching and KV cache hit rates.
[02:53] Maya: hmm balanced-int8 looks promising cost-wise. how about cost delta estimated?
[02:57] Priya: rough ballpark from our bench: compared to float16 baseline, balanced-int8 reduces token cost by ~45%, conservative-int8 ~35%, fp8 around 40% but depends on HW and kernel maturity. we'll include exact numbers in the pilot pricing sheet.
[03:15] Maya: ok great. can you show the fidelity comparison UI?
[03:18] Liam: sure — switching to the "Fidelity Lab". here you can upload a labeled prompt set, pick metrics (F1 on clinical entities, hallucination rate, rouge), and compare profiles side-by-side. i'm loading your sample set from last week. bear with me, the upload was anonymized by your team so labels are preserved.
[03:38] [03:40] Speaker 4: (unintelligible)
[03:43] Liam: looks like it's finished. here's a plot — at top we have hallucination rate: baseline fp16 3.2%, balanced-int8 4.1%, fp8 3.0%. entity F1: fp16 0.86, balanced-int8 0.81, fp8 0.84. overall you can pick a point on the curve for your acceptable tradeoff.
[04:06] Maya: those numbers align with our concerns. i guess fp8 gives us near-fp16 fidelity with a decent cost drop, but you mentioned concurrency risk?
[04:15] Liam: yes, memory layout for fp8 is trickier — some kernels are new and need more GPU memory headroom; on Dedicated pools you can reserve nodes with higher memory to avoid eviction. fallback policy in the routing layer will route to a compatible variant (e.g., balanced-int8) if capacity isn't available.
[04:34] Alex: can that fallback be per-tenant? we need consistent latencies for internal SLAs.
[04:39] Nora: you can set routing policy by customer tier; for ClearHealth we could pin primary route to fp8 but enable automatic fallback to balanced-int8 only for non-production routes. that gives prod consistency.
[04:52] Samir: on the private deployment side, does the console still show these options? we host in our VPC.
[04:58] Priya: yes, the Private control plane surfaces the same Optimize UI; logs are delivered to your SIEM, and the KMS integration works with your HSM. there are minor differences in kernel availability depending on underlying drivers, but we publish a compatibility matrix.
[05:14] Maya: what about a/b testing? can we route a percentage of traffic to fp8 to see live behavior?
[05:18] Liam: absolutely — we have canary rollouts: you define percent traffic, hold windows, automatic metrics checks for quality regressions, and auto rollback on a failure threshold. for pilot we'd recommend a 5% -> 20% -> 100% ramp with monitored hallucination and latency guards.
[05:36] Maya: nice. what counts as a failure trigger?
[05:38] Nora: you can set thresholds like hallucination rate +2% over baseline, or p95 latency +30% over baseline, and if triggered the rollout pauses or rolls back automatically.
[05:48] Alex: regarding benchmarks — you mentioned a 500-run sweep earlier that showed fp8 improvement. could we run a larger 1k sample sweep during the pilot?
[05:56] Priya: yes, that's the plan. Liam will run a 1k fidelity sweep including targeted hallucination checks and entity-level accuracy. results will be uploaded to the Fidelity Lab for your review.
[06:05] Liam: i'll also provide raw traces and token-level diffs so your audits can inspect changes.
[06:10] Samir: good — and please include the reproducibility hashes per run so we can tie them back to an audit.
[06:15] Liam: will do.
[06:17] Maya: switching gears — what about integration with our CI? we want to gate deployments if fidelity drops.
[06:22] Nora: the Console has a CLI and REST hooks; you can hook the fidelity test as a pre-deploy check. we also support webhooks that can pause rollouts.
[06:30] Alex: question on data residency — some notes must remain in-region. can routing be region-aware for inference?
[06:36] Priya: yes, you can pin routes to regions and configure fallback within the same region, or disable cross-region fallbacks entirely. for ClearHealth we can propose single-region private deployment in us-east-1.
[06:46] Maya: cost question again — for the pilot is there an option for a trial discount on fp8 nodes so we can test without a big commit?
[06:53] Priya: we can offer a time-limited pilot credit and reduced per-token rates for the pilot period; I'll include the proposed pricing in the sheet.
[06:59] Maya: thanks.
[07:01] [07:03] Speaker 2: (brief crosstalk)
[07:05] Liam: quick demo of console logs — here's a trace from a routed fp8 request showing quant profile id, kernel variant, and memory usage. note the trace includes the model sha and prompt hash.
[07:18] Alex: that trace view is helpful. what retention windows are available for these traces?
[07:22] Nora: up to 13 months on enterprise plans, shorter windows on hosted tiers. we can export to your S3/Blob storage for long-term retention.
[07:33] Samir: on SSO — we need SAML 2.0 with SCIM provisioning. is that supported?
[07:38] Priya: yes — SAML, SCIM, role-based access controls are all supported. we'll share our security pack with details including SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[07:47] Maya: any gotchas with model quantization that we should know when building tests? e.g., tokenization differences or prompt formatting sensitivity?
[07:55] Liam: tokenization isn't affected by quant per se, but small numeric differences can change early stop behavior; we recommend deterministic prompts with explicit stop tokens and include control tests for temperature/beam settings. also watch out for prefix caching — cache hits can mask quantization effects, so run both cold and warmed cache tests.
[08:15] Maya: good point about cache masking. can the Fidelity Lab simulate cold cache runs?
[08:19] Liam: yes, there's a toggle for cache state; you can run with KV cache disabled for baseline comparisons.
[08:24] Alex: for pilot we want both modes.
[08:26] Priya: makes sense. to summarize initial success criteria — net hallucination delta <= +1.5% versus your current baseline, p95 <= 200ms, and cost per 1k tokens reduced by at least 30%. does that sound reasonable?
[08:41] Maya: yes, those are good. Samir?
[08:43] Samir: fine as long as auditability + KMS integration is in place.
[08:47] Priya: ok next steps — we'll share pricing, security docs, pilot contract. Liam will run 1k sweep and upload results. Maya to share anonymized prompt sets. Alex to confirm peering window.
[08:59] [09:01] Speaker 3: (laughter)
[09:04] Maya: one more quick question — do you support model version pinning per route? we need to ensure rollbacks are simple.
[09:09] Nora: yes you can pin model version + quant profile, and we keep previous model/quant combos for quick rollback.
[09:16] Alex: timeline wise, can we aim to finish bench runs by 2026-06-15?
[09:20] Liam: yes that's doable.
[09:22] Priya: i'll send an invite for the pilot kickoff once we sign the pilot.
[09:26] Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:29] Priya: thanks all — we'll follow up with artifacts.
[09:33] [09:35] Meeting ended
